events.action: Interior Vice Minister Jang reported deployment of about 40 Seoul police, disarmament/arrest of 22 special-police personnel, recovery of 16 pistols, withdrawal of 7 guards, and recovery of 3 jeeps.
Kim Sang-deok told the Assembly that Interior Minister Yun Chi-young and the Special Committee had agreed to place about 20 directly usable special police personnel.
events.note: Contemporaneous parliamentary testimony; locate Interior Ministry agreement/personnel documents before upgrading.

events.action: Kim Sang-deok stated that the prime minister, interior minister and army chief discussed Rhee's special-police dissolution position and agreed to convert the personnel into ordinary police, with resumes to be supplied.
events.note: Date, minutes and implementation documents remain open.

events.action: Government reported mistaken receipt of some non-special-police documents followed by prompt return; committee leaders alleged broader document removal, movement restriction, communications interference and property seizure.

events.legal_authority: Anti-National Activities Special Investigation Organization Act plus appointment/administrative records still required
events.action: Interior Ministry argued no lawful police status existed without formal appointment; committee side argued prior Interior agreement and statutory investigative authority. Separate statutory judicial-police powers of investigation staff from the formal status of the separately named special police unit.

Assembly passed a shortening of the prosecution limitation period to the end of August 1949; treat as later institutional weakening with multiple causal factors rather than automatic direct consequence of the June 6 raid.
